findings.problem: Both primaries are the World Council of Churches' profile page of the Church of Greece. That page is the council's descriptive summary of another church, not the Church of Greece's or the Patriarchate's own text. Under the era 10 rule a summary never counts, and the WCC is not either body named on the link. Part 1 used WCC pages only for the council's own 'Member Since' record and its own history. With the profile set aside, the 1850 and 1928 facts rest on nothing read, and the link has only Frazee (1821-1852) and Leustean (1945-91), both named and not read. Neither covers the passage across 1906.
findings.evidence: Raw fetch of https://www.oikoumene.org/member-churches/church-of-greece (2026-11-10): both quotes are verbatim, inside the council's general profile ('The "Church of Greece" emerged with the founding of the autocephalous Orthodox Church in Greece in 1850 ... Christianity was first brought ... by the Apostle Paul'). It is a handbook-style profile, not a document of either church.
findings.fix: Preferred: replace the two WCC-profile primaries with a text of the Church of Greece or the Ecumenical Patriarchate read online (for example the 1850 Synodal Tomos or the 1928 Patriarchal and Synodal Act, or the Church of Greece's own history page), with quotes, and keep Widely Accepted. If none can be opened: remove the two WCC sources, regrade to Dominant Modern Reconstruction on Frazee (named, repo-cited), add the 1850 Tomos and the 1928 Act to wants, and replace the note with: "In 1850 a synod at Constantinople made the Church of Greece a church that ran itself. Charles Frazee's study of 1969 tells how that came about. The same church carried on into the new century." (FRE 75.2.)

findings.problem: Widely Accepted needs a secondary work for the consensus reading. The only secondary is Erickson, Orthodox Christians in America. It is not cited anywhere in the repo (grep finds no hit outside this audit folder) and was confirmed in this run only by an Open Library record. Under the era 10 rule such a study supports nothing beyond its title. So the grade has no secondary behind it, and the drafter's own flag says the grade rests on the two primaries alone. That is the case Open-Gaps 148 leaves open for Mark: a body's own text with no study.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'Orthodox Christians in America' records Build cic cic-website: 0 hits outside the part 2 folder. Open Library page fetched: bibliographic record only. Tomos (archdiocese.ca/node/298) and OCA history (oca.org) quotes verified verbatim by raw fetch.
findings.fix: Read and quote a passage of a study on the 1970 autocephaly (for example a preview page of Erickson, or any repo-cited history of the Metropolia), with url and accessed, and keep Widely Accepted. If no passage can be read, do not apply the link at Widely Accepted: hold it as a draft under Open-Gaps 148 (a body's own dated text with no study), and add Erickson's book to wants.

findings.problem: (a) The note's first fact, that the Lviv synod of March 1946 folded the Ukrainian church into the Russian Orthodox Church, is in no listed source that was read. The drafter says so. The only primary, the 2016 text, speaks of 'this gathering', its 'tragic decisions' and a 'pseudo-synod'. Widely Accepted needs a primary for the underlying facts. (b) The second and third sentences report the Ukrainian church's position in 2016 in the present tense ('calls', 'says'). That puts a post-2010 stance in a note. (c) 'the attacks on it that came after' is not in the text, which says only that the Moscow church 'was an instrument of persecution'. (d) The text is signed 'on behalf of the participants of the International Conference', so it is a conference statement, not the Moscow church's own text. The arrow runs from Moscow, but no Moscow text or act is on the link.
findings.evidence: Raw fetch of archives.ugcc.ua (2026-11-10): both quotes verbatim. The page is dated 'Tuesday, 29 March 2016' and signed 'Kyiv, 17 March 2016 On behalf of the participants of the International Conference ...'. No passage on the page states what the 1946 gathering decided.
findings.fix: Regrade to Dominant Modern Reconstruction resting on Bociurkiw (repo-cited, named). Keep the 2016 statement as a later source and flag its date. Replace the note with: "In March 1946 a synod at Lviv, held under Soviet rule, folded the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church into the Russian Orthodox Church. Bohdan Bociurkiw's study of the church and the Soviet state tells how it was done." (FRE 61.7, longest sentence 22 words). Put the 1946 sobor's own acts in wants.

But the longDescription's first sentence makes the same claim and has no disposition: 'Two communities, founded two years apart, that set out to be modern heirs of the old monastic ones.' An unsupported relationship claim is left standing as fact, and the entry now contradicts itself.

findings.fix: Add a 'qualify' disposition and replace the sentence with: "Two communities, founded two years apart, built a shared life of work and prayer." (FRE 71.8). Rescore the field.

findings.problem: The note calls Abdul Messiah II 'the patriarch of Antioch' in 1912 as plain fact. His standing in 1912 was disputed, and the drafter flags it. The only source read is the Malankara Orthodox side's own history. The note should say whose account it is. Major status and outcome are correct: the 1975 excommunication of the church's head, and the split that followed, meet step 4b (a church head excluded by an authority; a split into two bodies).

Unfortunately, this led to a schism ...'; '... in 1975 ... an excommunication from the Patriarch of Antioch of His Holiness Catholicos Baselios Augen, which led to the creation of two factions again.'
findings.fix: Replace the note's first sentence with: "The Malankara Orthodox Church's own history says that in 1912 Patriarch Abdul Messiah II made Baselios Paulose I its head." Keep the rest. The note scores FRE 66.6.

findings.problem: major.kind is 'council-law', but Ad Apostolorum Principis is a papal encyclical, not a council or canon. Part 1's review made the same point on Mortalium Animos (R1-17). The major call and the outcome are correct. Section 39 rules that bishops consecrated against Rome's orders have no power to teach or govern, which is a ruling that excludes a group.

findings.evidence: Sacrosanctum Concilium art. 21 and art. 36.2, raw fetch, verbatim.
findings.fix: Replace the outcome with: "The council called for a general restoration of the liturgy. It also let people use their own language more often in the Mass and the sacraments." (FRE 60.2).

checks.major_calls: Malankara and Antioch 1975: major, correct (a church head excommunicated and a split). Georgia and Russia 1943, resting on a study's report: acceptable. Step 4b asks that one of the link's own listed sources show the act, and a study read online is a listed source. Dominant Modern Reconstruction is the right grade. Georgian tomos: major, correct. The study's timing ('immediately after the collapse of the Soviet Union', under Demetrios I, who died in October 1991) is wrong on its own terms, and the note rightly gives no year. Pius X to Chinese Catholicism: major, correct (R1-8 on kind only). Tridentine to post-Vatican II at Widely Accepted on Summorum Pontificum: correct. The 2007 law is itself the act, Art. 2 changes a rule, the 1570 bull is held in the Library, and the 2007 date is inside 2010. Anglican to Philippine Independent Church: major, correct. The church's supreme bodies formally adopted the Declaration on Binsted's advice and set aside the 1903 rules (art. 20). That is a rule changed by an authority, not a text merely taken up. Liturgical movement to post-Vatican II: major, correct (R1-9 on wording). Judged minor and agreed: liturgical movement to Pius X (Mediator Dei warns and restates the rubrics), Russian church to the Ukrainian underground (no listed source shows the act), Pius X church to Latin America (CELAM set up at the bishops' request), and post-Vatican II to Latin America.
checks.later_papal_texts: Benedict XVI 2005 (CELAM 1955), John Paul II 1999 (1899 to 1968) and the CBCP 2007 (Barlin 1902-06) are each the body's own dated official statement about its own past. That fits the letter of the rule (an official statement), and each sits beside a named secondary, so Widely Accepted holds. They are recollections, not documents of the time. The CELAM founding decree and the 1899 council's acts would be stronger, and belong on wants. Summorum Pontificum 2007 is a primary for its own 2007 act, not for earlier events.
